title: INFQ Stock Surges After Infleqtion Solves Key Technical Hurdle In Large-Scale Quantum Computing
key_facts: Infleqtion, a US neutral-atom quantum computing company listed on NYSE as INFQ, said it entangled 30 logical qubits using 80 physical qubits, announced at Quantum World Congress 2026 on a Thursday.
The company calls itself the first neutral-atom quantum company to reach 30 logical qubits on a commercial system; the signal was about 1,000 times stronger than the noise.
Logical qubits combine several physical qubits with error correction to hold information more reliably.
Infleqtion says the result validates its Sqale processor and Superstaq software; an AI-assisted discovery halved the physical gates needed for a key logical operation.
Shares rose 3.4 percent on Thursday and kept climbing after hours; retail sentiment on Stocktwits turned 'extremely bullish'.

Background: Q2 revenue of 12.6 million dollars (up 116 percent), a proposed up to 100 million dollar US Commerce Department agreement, and a contract for a fault-tolerant machine in Illinois in 2027; it went public via SPAC in February raising over 550 million dollars.
quote_evidence: Infleqtion shares surged 3.4% on Thursday and extended the climb overnight after the quantum computing company announced it had successfully entangled 30 logical qubits using just 80 physical qubits.
Infleqtion said its 30 logical qubits were entangled into a single coherent quantum state, with the signal measuring approximately 1,000 times stronger than the underlying noise.
In a statement Thursday, the company said the result validates the architecture of its Sqale quantum processing platform and Superstaq software.
why_it_matters_hint: A low physical-to-logical qubit ratio is the core scaling problem; this is a company claim with no outside review reported.
event_date: Article says Thursday, most likely 1 Oct 2026; feed date 3 Oct 2026
notes: Company claim relayed by Stocktwits, a retail-trading news site; no peer review or independent check mentioned. The headline's 'solves key technical hurdle' overstates a single demonstration. Internal dating (Thursday) conflicts with the 3 Oct feed timestamp, so treated as a follow-up of 1 Oct 2026.
